properties.decision:
`ifc:graph-read` keeps designation `internal`. It is a real modular boundary — modules are swapped, tested and measured across it — but it is NOT a contract this design offers to anyone else.

THE TEST THAT DECIDED IT, and it is the test to re-apply rather than the answer to re-quote: is anybody outside this project's control writing code against these five functions? Anthony, 2026-08-21: "nobody writing code against those five functions."

THE STRUCTURAL FACTS BEHIND THAT ANSWER, checked rather than assumed:
  — `reflow2-core` is not published as a crate; it is not on crates.io.
  — its only dependant is `reflow2-mcp`, by local path, inside the same workspace.
  — users receive released binaries and speak MCP. They never link the library, so they could not call `GraphRead` if they wanted to.

MODULAR IS NOT THE SAME AS PUBLISHED, and conflating them is what this decision refuses. A modular system holds many internal boundaries and publishes the few where somebody else is meant to supply the part. Publishing every boundary means nothing can change without a control board; publishing none means nobody can compete to supply anything. The graph read API is how reflow2's own analysis reads its own store — not a part a second supplier is wanted for.

WHAT PUBLISHING WOULD HAVE COST: the boundary would enter the surface reflow2 shows other designs, other projects' tooling would pair against it, and adding a sixth operation would become a breaking change to a recorded promise instead of an ordinary edit.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS — two triggers, either sufficient:
  (1) `reflow2-core` is published as a crate for others to build on.
  (2) an implementation is wanted from somebody other than this project — a different store, a hosted backend.
Neither holds today, and the designation is one call to change if one starts to.

📌 NOT SETTLED HERE: `ifc:core-api` is marked `published` and fails the same test — a Rust library API, in the same undistributed crate, covering the whole 274-function surface rather than a specified subset. That is a larger question about what this project has already committed to, and it is open.
properties.name: DECIDED — the graph read contract stays internal, because nobody outside can call it
properties.rationale:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-21, answering the deciding question directly: nobody is writing code against those five functions.

RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A DEFAULT. `internal` is what an Interface is until someone says otherwise, so the designation alone cannot distinguish "considered and declined" from "nobody ever looked" — the same two-states-look-identical problem this whole week has been about. Without this node a later reader finds a carefully specified contract sitting at the default value and cannot tell which it is.

THE HONEST HISTORY: it was set to `published` first, on the reasoning that reflow2's own tooling calls `published` the MOSA modular-system-interface distinction and Anthony's goal is modularity. That was reverted before anyone was asked, because publishing is a commitment and the tool says so plainly — and asserting a commitment on the owner's behalf is exactly what `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` forbids. The reversal was the right act; this decision is the part that was owed after it.
